Map of Africa in 1914, colour-coded by colonial power. The map shows British territories in red (e.g., Nigeria, Gold Coast, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt), French in blue (e.g., French West Africa, Madagascar, Algeria), Portuguese in green (Angola, Mozambique, Guinea-Bissau), Belgian in yellow (Belgian Congo), German in grey (Togo, Kamerun, German East Africa, German South-West Africa), Spanish in orange (Rio de Oro, Equatorial Guinea), and Italian in purple (Libya, Somalia). Ethiopia and Liberia remain uncoloured (independent).

Split illustration showing Indirect Rule vs Direct Rule. On the left (Indirect Rule): A British officer in a khaki uniform sitting beside a traditional Emir on a throne; the Emir is giving orders to his subjects while the British officer watches. On the right (Direct Rule): A French colonial officer standing directly in front of a group of African villagers, giving them orders himself, while a traditional chief stands passively in the background.
